name: eIDAS Regulation
evidence_rating: thin but direct: Commission evaluation with usage counts and cost-benefit baseline; no independent quantitative or causal studies
summary: eIDAS aimed to let people use their national e-ID and e-signatures across the EU. The Commission's 2021 evaluation found trust services such as qualified e-signatures took off (202 qualified providers), but cross-border e-ID use was tiny - at most tens of thousands of logins a year per country - so costs exceeded benefits. Notification has since spread to 24 of 27 countries, and the 2024 revision (European Digital Identity Wallet) is meant to fix low uptake; no independent study measures economic effects.

indicators.objective: Enhance trust in pan-European electronic transactions and ensure cross-border legal recognition of electronic identification, authentication, signature and related trust services

indicators.indicator: Electronic identification schemes notified to the Commission
indicators.evidence: Measured: 19 schemes from 14 Member States by early 2021, covering 59% of the EU population. Commission list (updated Feb 2026) shows notified schemes for 24 of 27 Member States (none for Greece, Hungary, Ireland), plus Liechtenstein and Norway.

indicators.indicator: Extent to which eIAS are used by end-users for national and cross-border transactions
indicators.evidence: Measured once: 100 to 30,000 successful cross-border authentications a year, against millions domestically; only 14% of seven key public services for cross-border users offered eIDAS login (2020). No later series found.

indicators.indicator: Services accessible with notified eID in the public and private sector
indicators.evidence: Public: 67% of Member States could accept notified eIDs (2020). Private: 17 Member States had a national eID open to private providers but only 12 had notified one; evaluation found private-sector use very limited.

indicators.indicator: Existence of eIAS suppliers active in multiple Member States
indicators.evidence: 202 active qualified trust service providers in 29 of 30 EU/EEA countries (2021), concentrated in Spain, France, Italy, Germany; evaluation found take-up of trust services increased but supervision and interpretation still diverge.
Evaluation's baseline cost-benefit analysis: quantifiable costs so far higher than benefits, because eID uptake was too low for benefits to materialise; costs fall mainly on public authorities.

literature.citation: European Commission (2012), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a Regulation on electronic identification and trust services for electronic transactions in the internal market (executive summary SWD(2012) 136), SWD(2012) 135
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a Regulation on electronic identification and trust services for electronic transactions in the internal market (executive summary SWD(2012) 136)
literature.headline: Preferred option (comprehensive framework incl. ancillary trust services) expected to boost availability and take-up of cross-border eID and trust services; executive summary gives no monetised benefit estimate
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected one EU framework for e-ID and e-signatures to remove barriers to secure online transactions across borders, but did not put a number on the gains.

literature.citation: European Commission (2021), Report on the evaluation of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 (eIDAS), COM(2021) 290
literature.title: Report on the evaluation of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 (eIDAS)
literature.outcomes: eID coverage and uptake; trust services; costs and benefits
literature.headline: Regulation has not achieved its potential on eID: notified eIDs cover 59% of population, acceptance limited, quantifiable costs higher than benefits due to low uptake; trust services: legal certainty achieved, take-up increased, market fragmentation reduced but no full level playing field
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's own evaluation found the e-signature and trust-service rules worked reasonably well, but the cross-border e-ID part had so little use that its costs exceeded its benefits.

literature.citation: European Commission (2021), Staff Working Document accompanying the evaluation of the eIDAS Regulation, SWD(2021) 130
literature.title: Staff Working Document accompanying the evaluation of the eIDAS Regulation
literature.method: ex-post evaluation; stakeholder surveys; cost-benefit analysis based on stakeholder estimates
literature.outcomes: trust service market; private-sector eID use; costs
literature.headline: 202 active qualified trust service providers in 29 of 30 EU/EEA countries; only 12 Member States notified eID schemes usable by private providers; costs borne mainly by public authorities, benefits mainly by users and market operators; data dispersion large
literature.summary_plain: Detailed evaluation: a real EU market for qualified trust services emerged (202 providers), but private companies hardly use national e-IDs across borders.

literature.citation: European Commission (presentation to Council Telecom Working Party) (2021), Revision of the eIDAS Regulation - European Digital Identity: evaluation preliminary results, Council document WK 163/2021, 7 Jan 2021
literature.authors: European Commission (presentation to Council Telecom Working Party)
literature.title: Revision of the eIDAS Regulation - European Digital Identity: evaluation preliminary results
literature.headline: 19 notified schemes from 14 Member States (59% of population); 67% of Member States can accept notified eIDs; 14% of key cross-border public services offer eIDAS login; 100-30,000 successful cross-border authentications a year vs millions domestically
literature.summary_plain: Cross-border logins with national e-IDs numbered only between a hundred and thirty thousand a year per country, against millions of domestic logins.

literature.citation: European Commission (eID User Community) (2026), Overview of pre-notified and notified eID schemes under eIDAS, Commission web page, last updated 2 Feb 2026
literature.title: Overview of pre-notified and notified eID schemes under eIDAS
literature.venue: Commission web page, last updated 2 Feb 2026
literature.headline: Notified schemes listed for 24 of 27 Member States (first: Germany 2017; latest additions Romania 2024, France Identite 2024, Finland 2025); no notified scheme for Greece, Hungary or Ireland
literature.summary_plain: By 2026, 24 of 27 EU countries had notified a national e-ID for cross-border use, up from 14 in 2021.

literature.citation: Lips, Bharosa & Draheim (2020), eIDAS Implementation Challenges: The Case of Estonia and the Netherlands, Communications in Computer and Information Science vol. 1349 (EGOSE 2020), Springer
literature.title: eIDAS Implementation Challenges: The Case of Estonia and the Netherlands
literature.venue: Communications in Computer and Information Science vol. 1349 (EGOSE 2020), Springer
literature.headline: Compares eIDAS implementation in two digitally advanced countries; finds the regulation raised many practical questions and identifies research gaps
literature.summary_plain: A comparison of Estonia and the Netherlands shows that even digital front-runners struggled with practical questions in applying eIDAS.
